note: Session and pull request facts were checked against GitHub (PRs, issues, branches) and the local .sessions*.json launch files.

sessions.outcome: Proposed 8 hostile network scenarios (structured output saved in docs/scout_scenarios.json). No code, no PR.
Proposed 8 scenarios about ids, Lamport values and text (docs/scout_scenarios.json). No code, no PR.
Proposed 8 scenarios about tabs, storage, restarts and clocks (docs/scout_scenarios.json). No code, no PR.

Built chaos/, a deterministic simulation of the 24 scout scenarios plus one control run (25 in all), with regression tests. Its runs showed 8 scenarios failing. The playbook asked for a separate fix pull request per failure; none was opened, so the failures were pinned as strict expected failures.
Four Learn stages and learn/grader.py. Merged, then partly overridden: its write grader accepted `import os`, so the sandbox was rewritten by hand (see Rejected or overridden work).
server/learn_api.py: gated reference-code reveal, per-learner progress, capped and rate-limited writes. Merged.
Referee Race: server/race_api.py, client/race.*, board tab. Merged.

Drove the app in a browser, filed 5 issues with screenshots and pushed branch devin/qa-fixes (3 fix commits and a screenshots commit). It opened no pull request and wrote no docs/QA.md. Two of the three fixes were cherry-picked by hand; the screenshots stay on the branch because the issues link to them.

rejected_or_overridden: LEARN-CONTENT's write grader (PR #5) only blocked imports of the project's own modules. A submitted function that imported os could write a file on the host. It was replaced by hand with an AST check, a builtins whitelist and resource limits.

A later blind review found the replacement was still escapable: the learner's function ran inside the ledger module's namespace, where `json` was visible, and `json.codecs.sys.modules["os"]` passed the AST check. That was also fixed by hand: the function now runs in a fresh namespace that holds only ledger symbols (tests/test_learn_sandbox.py has the exact probe as a regression test). The Learn write endpoint is still closed to the LAN by default.

QA-RECORD's branch devin/qa-fixes was never turned into a pull request. Its client fix for two tabs and for half-typed notes was cherry-picked, then changed: a tab now takes over only operations it has never seen, so a stale record cannot undo a resync.
QA-RECORD's third fix commit (install segno in run.sh and CI) was not cherry-picked because main already had the CI fix; run.sh was fixed separately.

WRITER-chaos-sim reported 8 failing scenarios but opened no fix pull requests. All of the fixes (cursor and reset, re-stamping refused Lamport times, two tabs, a fresh id for a reused id, most of the restore-from-backup cases) were written by hand. Three scenarios are still open (see README).
No Devin pull request was rejected outright; all five were merged by a human pressing merge. Two of the five (the chaos harness and the Learn grader) needed substantial human rework afterwards.
acu_note: Not recorded, and not claimed. The Devin API has not been queried: no Devin token was available in the environment where this page was last updated. The earlier live snapshot (git-ignored data/devin_counts.json) reported 0.0, which means 'not reported', not zero. Each session was launched with an ACU cap: 3 by default (ops/devin_client.py) and 5 for the sessions started by ops/launch_extra.py, so the most any session could have used is capped, but the actual figure is unknown. To fill it in: run `python -m ops.devin_counts <env file> 30` with a Devin token and copy the figure here.
share_of_work: Devin wrote the scenario list (three read-only scouts), the first version of the chaos harness, and the Learn, Race and board-tab scaffolding. A human wrote the merge function, the referee, the server, the phone client, the sync protocol fixes, the sandbox that finally held, and every bug fix the harness provoked. The chat shell, the heart-rate engine, the live Devin bridge, the built-in course and the integration that made the chat the root page were not produced by any of these nine cloud sessions and are not credited to Devin. Counting sessions or pull requests overstates how much of the hard part Devin did.
